text: This is the shape of 10391, which you confirmed as a clear example of 10kKO, here with one extra Black fill at a, which costs nothing if Black plays it first, like the free moves in 10393. Then both sides need the same move, at b or c, and whoever plays it hands the other side a free take that threatens at once: Black's investment in Diagram 2, White's in Diagram 3. So the tree's S[10kKO] is right, and Black needs one threat more than White.

The solver said KO− because its line counts Black's investment, Black 15 in Diagram 2, as preparation and reads only the ko after it. To print 10kKO here, it must also treat Black's fill at a as free.

text: At the leaf White's best move is to take the ko at once: if White waits, Black approaches first and needs only one threat. White 16's capture threatens to take four stones, so Black must retake with a threat (Diagram 2), and Black 17 threatens nothing yet, since White still has two outside liberties. Black needs one approach, White retakes for free after it, and Black needs a second threat. So White took first, and Black needs two threats more than White: S[A-1KO-], the form you chose for c121.

The tree's S[A-1KO ] has a trailing space, which besogo trims; it then reads A-1KO+: Black takes first and needs one threat more. With one threat more than White, Black fails in both search areas (Diagram 3). Both reviewers agree with S[A-1KO-]. Change it together with the E16 leaf below: without that change, the site would mark Black 15 wrong.

Black must approach at A14 and keep E16 for the capture, where White can never extend. White 18 in Diagram 2 plays elsewhere, as the label counts it: by your c121 rule, what White gains with that free move belongs to the approach. With White's best free moves, Black needs four threats more in the narrow search area; in the wider one the count stayed undecided.

text: White 16 has just taken the ko, the line's first ko capture: Black 13 kept two liberties when it captured. White's capture threatens at once: if Black does not retake, White captures four stones and lives. Black 17's retake threatens nothing yet, since White still has two outside liberties. Black needs one approach, White retakes for free after it, and Black needs a second threat (Diagram 2). So White took first, and Black needs two threats more than White: S[A-1KO-], the form you chose for c121.

The tree's S[A-1KO ] has a trailing space, which besogo trims; it then reads A-1KO+: Black takes first and needs one threat more. With one threat more than White, Black fails in both search areas (Diagram 3). Both reviewers agree with S[A-1KO-]. Change it together with the E16 leaf below: without that change, the site would mark Black 15 wrong.

Black must approach at F19 and keep E16 for the capture, where White can never extend. White 18 in Diagram 2 plays elsewhere, as the label counts it; White's best free move there is the extension at F19, and by your c121 rule that gain belongs to the approach. With it, Black needs four threats more in the narrow search area; in the wider one the count stayed undecided.

Set S[A-1KO-2] on the E16 leaf, Black 15 in Diagram 1, the third answer beside the two fixed leaves: its S[A-1KO] has the same error (Other leaves to check in this tree, below). That is the label by your c121 rule; by the full count it would get the same S[] as its siblings. Without this change, the two fixes would make the site reject the other two answers (On the site, below).
Optional, not needed for the grading: add White's take, White 16, under it, as the A14 branch already has, and put the S[] on White 16.

text: With the two fixes alone, the site marks a and b in Diagram 1 wrong, and White's take under a with them; today both are correct. The grading check found these new marks wrong: a and b lose their mark only because their sibling c keeps its S[A-1KO], which besogo reads as A-1KO+, and c has the same error. So fix c as well (Change the tree as well, above).

With c at S[A-1KO-2], the label by your c121 rule, only c turns wrong, and the problem's result becomes A-1KO−: c needs one threat more than a and b, because after c White can extend at either remaining liberty. Giving c the same S[] as a and b, as all three need four threats in the narrow area, changes no mark; but that is a label by the full count (question 4), against your c121 rule. Black's two correct answers at move 5 keep their mark either way, since leaf k026 keeps S[10kKO].

text: The grading checker found one more leaf, Black 15 in Diagram 1, marked S[A-1KO]. White takes first, and Black needs one approach, at a or b. Whichever of the two Black leaves for last, White extends there when Black's next retake puts it in atari; Black must fill again, and White retakes for free (Diagrams 2 and 3). That extension answers a threatening retake, so it stays in the label under your c121 rule, as White's local threat: S[A-1KO-2], three threats. Black 15 at a or b instead keeps E16 for the capture and needs two.

The tree's S[] is wrong under every reading: with one threat more than White, Black fails in both search areas, and both reviews of the check agree. The exact S[] is less settled. Read as a second approach (question 3), Black's extra fill gives S[A-2KO-], which grades the same. By the full count all three answers need four threats in the narrow area, so a label by the count (question 4) gives this leaf its siblings' S[]. The research missed the leaf because the solver left its direct ko undecided.
